subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class session archive/rotation event that cron can subscribe to, or keep this as a plugin/internal-hook pattern?
rationale: The request crosses session state, cron dispatch, plugin boundaries, and security permissions, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API contract by itself.

options.title: Design core event contract
options.body: Add a durable session lifecycle event with scoped metadata, cron matching, permission checks, and trace links before implementation.

options.title: Keep it in plugins/hooks
options.body: Document or extend plugin hooks if maintainers want this outside core and do not need cron schedule syntax.

options.title: Decline event-driven cron
options.body: Keep polling or new-session startup workarounds if maintainers decide the security and complexity cost is not worth the core surface.

recommendation.title: Design core event contract
recommendation.body: Add a durable session lifecycle event with scoped metadata, cron matching, permission checks, and trace links before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout history points to Peter Steinberger for the relevant cron/session lifecycle files and the decision spans core architecture boundaries.
